protocol.scenario_set: all integer triples (N0,N1,N2) with each Ni>=500, sum=10000, and every Ni on a 500-count lattice
protocol.objective: maximize the minimum expected correct specificity across all 171 finite-population scenarios
protocol.conditional_test_type_weights: residual population after the calibration count vector
protocol.risk_constraints: all 1,378 augmented count vectors, independent of scenario weights

interpretation: The nominal oracle utility policy loses almost all specificity on the extreme mixture (500,9000,500), despite remaining risk-valid.
The robust maximin policy preserves a specificity floor of about 1.44543% across the 171-scenario grid.
Equal-share has essentially the same worst-case specificity floor; the difference is below solver tolerance. It appears maximin-optimal for this grid and common-depth family.
The value of the robust optimizer here is protection against nominal objective misspecification, not an improvement over equal-share.
The LP risk constraints cover all augmented states, not only the 171 scenarios.
limitations: the set is a 5-percentage-point lattice, not the continuous simplex
no guarantee for mixtures outside the finite grid
finite-exchangeability expected-risk guarantee only, not a shift-robust risk theorem
common-depth only; no per-image confidence adaptation
exact committed source/tests not yet executed in a clean checkout
